slides.title: Why Semantic Table Elements? 🧠
slides.content:
# More Than Just `<tr>` and `<td>`

Large tables can be divided into logical sections:
- `<thead>` – header rows (usually the first row(s) with column titles).
- `<tbody>` – the main body of data.
- `<tfoot>` – footer rows (summary, totals).

These help screen readers navigate and allow CSS to target specific parts. They also let the browser repeat headers when printing long tables.

quizData.question: Which section should hold the column titles of a table?
quizData.explanation: <thead> is designated for header rows, containing <th> elements.

slides.title: The `<caption>` Element 📝
slides.content:
# Give Your Table a Title `` is placed directly inside `` (before any row) and provides a title for the entire table. ```html
...
Student Grades – Spring 2025
``` It appears above the table by default, but can be repositioned with CSS. Screen readers associate it with the table for context.

slides.title: Column Groups with `<colgroup>` and `<col>` 📏
slides.content:
# Style or Target Columns Efficiently You can define styles for entire columns without repeating classes on every cell. ```html ...
Name Score Grade
``` `` can have `span` to cover multiple columns. Use it for applying background colours, widths, or visibility to entire columns.

quizData.question: The `<caption>` tag must be placed after the `<thead>` section.
quizData.explanation: `<caption>` is placed immediately after the opening `<table>` tag, before any rows or sections.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Include `<thead>`

Even if you don't need `<tfoot>`, wrapping your header row(s) in `<thead>` is a small effort that greatly improves accessibility and maintainability.
